q: How do I calculate the carbon footprint of a flush door?
title: Flush door carbon footprint per door
short: Add the timber or block board core, face veneers or laminates and adhesive per door with supplier figures. Add hot press, sanding and finishing energy, then divide the plant's energy by doors made, stated by size and thickness.

ul: Core: solid timber, block board or particle board.
Face veneers, plywood skins or laminates.
Adhesive, usually urea or phenol formaldehyde.
Hot press, often heated by a wood or oil fired boiler.
Polish or paint if supplied finished.

p: Report per door with size and thickness. Wood waste burned in the boiler still counts toward boiler fuel use.

example.title: Worked example: flush door unit per door (one month)
lines: Plant total: 19,560 / 8,000 = 2.445 kg CO2 per door
Add core, skins and adhesive for the full figure
example.note: Inputs are illustrative; use your own bills and production records.

senseible: Senseible reads the plant's electricity bills (CEA grid factor 0.710 kg CO2 per kWh, CO2 Baseline Database version 21.0) and fuel invoices (IPCC 2006 defaults) into a fingerprinted Scope 1 and 2 record, the plant-level input to a per-unit figure. Bought-in materials go to the supplier evidence trail; product reports are self-declared drafts.
